clue.text: With physical training, is able to secure the nut

parts.note: PE is the usual abbreviation for physical education or training at school
is able means can

explanation.surface: Gym exercise gives someone the strength to crack a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-shelled kernel from a hickory tree of the American south, so a kind of nut.

clue.text: Little Women -at the tea-table?

parts.note: read Little as French small and Women as the four March sisters of the novel, then find a tiny fancy cake served with tea

explanation.surface: The March sisters of the novel sitting down to tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcott's novel Little Women follows four sisters, so 'Little Women' playfully becomes small (French) plus the number of women.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite-sized iced cake or biscuit served at afternoon tea, French for small oven.

clue.text: Charles Martel's first big difference of opinion

parts.note: Chas is the standard short written form of the name Charles

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of Martel's is wanted

explanation.surface: Charles Martel, the Frankish leader, had a major disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Martel was an eighth-century Frankish ruler; the surface treats his name as one, but it splits into Charles and the first letter of Martel.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep gulf, used figuratively for a wide rift between people's views.

clue.text: Botanist, no longer a student, likes life in the raw

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does this

indicators.note: no longer says a piece is dropped from the botanist word, here the student and article

parts.note: a botanist studies plants, so is a kind of naturalist
A plus L, the learner-driver letter that crosswords use for a student

explanation.surface: A plant scientist who has finished studying takes to going without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the raw' is an idiom for naked. The definition describes what the person does rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist enjoys going about unclothed, which is living in the raw.

clue.text: Letters not written in Rome or Paris

definitions.text: Letters not written in Rome or Paris

parts.words: Letters not written in Rome or Paris
parts.note: Rome and Paris are capitals, so letters not written in capitals are the small ones of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Correspondence that was never posted from Italy or France.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests letters as mail and cities abroad; the trick is that Rome and Paris are capitals, standing for capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters of the alphabet, as opposed to capitals, named after the printer's lower tray of type.

clue.text: Does the conductor play first?

definitions.meaning: does what a conductor does: directs or guides an orchestra or band
in card games, to put down the opening card of a trick

explanation.surface: Is the orchestra's director also the one who starts?
explanation.definitionFit: To guide or direct performers, and in bridge to open a trick with the first card.

clue.text: Ask me why it makes a mannerly man

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the preceding words are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what produces a well-behaved gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: A WYKEHAMIST is a pupil of Winchester College, an English private school whose motto is 'Manners makyth man', which the surface echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or old boy of Winchester College, whose motto claims that manners make the man.

clue.text: Put on more polish and brush off

definitions.meaning: to buff again, giving a shoe or surface a further shine
to reject or snub someone curtly

explanation.surface: Polish the shoes again and sweep the dust away.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves look like shoe-cleaning, but 'brush off' means a curt rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-buff it is polishing again; as one word it is a blunt refusal or snub.

clue.text: Freak rain storm in the Transvaal, perhaps

definitions.note: stands for a person found there, a description rather than a noun

indicators.note: storm signals the letters are thrown about violently into a new order

explanation.surface: An unusual downpour hits a South African province.
explanation.walkthrough: The Transvaal was a province of South Africa, heavily settled by Dutch-descended farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afrikaans-speaking white South African of Dutch descent, many of whom lived in that province.

clue.text: Winter and rough weather the only one in Arden.

definitions.text: Winter and rough weather the only one in Arden.

parts.words: Winter and rough weather the only one in Arden.
parts.note: a song in As You Like It, set in the Forest of Arden, says there you shall see no foe but winter and rough weather

explanation.surface: In the Forest of Arden the only hardship is the bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's song 'Under the greenwood tree' runs 'Here shall he see no enemy but winter and rough weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe or adversary; the song says the weather is the sole one in the forest.

clue.text: Drink stand makes a popular wedding gift

parts.note: to drink a toast, raising glasses to someone
a rack is a stand or frame for holding things

explanation.surface: A raised glass and a stand make a good wedding present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' and 'stand' sound like the wedding reception, but they supply the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakfast holder for slices of grilled bread, once a traditional present for newlyweds.

clue.text: Vessel that needs a push

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed boat for canal or river freight
to shove or bump one's way roughly

explanation.surface: A boat that has to be shoved along.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed river boat, and as a verb to shove or barge rudely into someone.

clue.text: The turning of the wood at the end shows sound quality

indicators.note: turning says letters are swung round to face the other way
at the end limits the turning to the final pair of letters of the wood word

parts.note: timber is wood used for building

explanation.surface: Wood-turning finishes off with a fine ring to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The turning of the wood' suggests a lathe; only the last two letters of TIMBER swap round, ER becoming RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive tone colour of a voice or instrument, separate from pitch or loudness.

clue.text: As long as 4 is needed, it won't get depressed

definitions.text: As long as 4 is needed, it won't get depressed

parts.words: As long as 4 is needed, it won't get depressed
parts.note: while only small letters are typed, the keyboard key for capitals is never pressed down

explanation.surface: Someone who stays cheerful so long as they are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 refers to 4 across, small letters. 'Depressed' looks like low spirits but means pressed down on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The typewriter or keyboard button held down to type capitals.

clue.text: Scientist like Flamsteed with a royal following

definitions.text: Scientist like Flamsteed with a royal following

parts.words: Scientist like Flamsteed with a royal following
parts.note: John Flamsteed was the first to hold the title in which the word royal comes after his profession

explanation.surface: A scientist with a band of royal fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Flamsteed was the first Astronomer Royal at Greenwich; 'royal following' means the word Royal follows in the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies stars and planets; Flamsteed was the first Royal one at Greenwich.

clue.text: Magical words that make sense in a poem perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Words with magic in them make sense when found in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the two fodder pieces SENSE and A POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The password that opens the robbers' cave in Ali Baba, a classic spell.

clue.text: Oculist's report that could turn your head

definitions.meaning: a verdict that a patient's vision is fine
a drill command telling marching soldiers to look to one side

explanation.surface: An eye doctor's findings could leave you looking round.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean bill of health for vision, and a parade-ground order to look sideways.

clue.text: 6 turned up

definitions.meaning: the answer to 6 down, a curt brush-off

explanation.surface: A clue number that appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate slight, and the word for a short nose tilted upwards.

clue.text: The foremost 'rider could be roused into action

parts.note: the foremost means the best, the leading one

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of rider may become something else

explanation.surface: The leading jockey might be stirred into activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges RIDER into IRRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred oneself up, got moving after being idle.

clue.text: His job may include looking after the royal pens

definitions.text: His job may include looking after the royal pens

parts.words: His job may include looking after the royal pens
parts.note: pens are female swans, and the British monarch owns many swans on the Thames

explanation.surface: A clerk in charge of the King's writing implements.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan; 'pens' suggests writing tools. Unmarked swans on the Thames belong to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of swans, tending the birds rather than stationery.

clue.text: Regretted sounding discourteous

indicators.note: sounding signals that a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: discourteous means rude

explanation.surface: Was sorry for coming across as impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt sorrow or remorse over something done.

clue.text: These squares, though full of lights, may be obscure in places

definitions.text: These squares, though full of lights, may be obscure in places

parts.words: These squares, though full of lights, may be obscure in places
parts.note: grids of squares whose entries are called lights, with clues that are often baffling

explanation.surface: Town squares, brightly lit, may still have dark corners.
explanation.walkthrough: In puzzle jargon a light is an answer entered in the grid, so these lit squares are puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Word puzzles set in a grid whose answers are called lights.

clue.text: More than one platoon on the mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: PL is the military abbreviation for platoon
the Ural range dividing Europe from Asia

explanation.surface: Soldiers out on a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical form for several of something, not singular.

clue.text: Fauntleroy

parts.note: the title character of Little Lord Fauntleroy, a boy who becomes heir to an earldom

explanation.definitionFit: A minor or young noble, the little peer of Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel.

clue.text: Skipped field-exercise

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Missed out on the outdoor drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumped or bounded, past tense of a verb for springing.

clue.text: Much in Cubism gives one nightmares

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the plural demons who do this

indicators.note: much, meaning most of, says only part of the words in Cubism is used

explanation.surface: A great deal of abstract art is the stuff of bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' takes most of IN CUBISM, dropping the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil spirits said to lie on sleepers, causing bad dreams.

clue.text: Advocate finishing off the beef cake

indicators.note: finishing off here means the opening letter of the beef cake word is knocked off

parts.note: a burger is a patty or cake of minced beef

explanation.surface: A supporter polishes off the meat patty.
explanation.definitionFit: One who presses for or champions something.

clue.text: Detect first sign of enemy agent

indicators.note: first sign of picks out the opening letter of enemy

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Spotting the earliest hint of a hostile operative.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of or spot something.

clue.text: Dropping a £100 brick causes annoyance

indicators.note: dropping says letters fall out of the brick word

parts.note: dropping a brick or a clanger are British idioms for an embarrassing blunder
L for pound (from libra) and C for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone who drops a costly brick ends up irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'drop a brick' or 'drop a clanger' is British for making a gaffe; CLANGER loses C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritation or displeasure, a feeling of being cross.

clue.text: Obviously the runner for the relay?

definitions.text: Obviously the runner for the relay?

parts.words: Obviously the runner for the relay?
parts.note: relaying a message is the job of one who carries word, not a sprinter in a baton race

explanation.surface: Picking the athlete for the relay race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'relay' suggest athletics, but to relay is to pass on news.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier who carries news or word from one person to another.

clue.text: "Long time no see". says the bishop appointed thus?

definitions.text: "Long time no see". says the bishop appointed thus?

parts.words: "Long time no see". says the bishop appointed thus?
parts.note: a bishop holding the rank in name only has no diocese, so for him there is no see at all

explanation.surface: A bishop greets an old friend with a familiar phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; a titular bishop bears the title of an extinct see and has none to govern.
explanation.definitionFit: In name only, holding a title without the real duties or territory.

clue.text: Dread being wrongly challenged

indicators.note: wrongly indicates the letters are put in an incorrect order

explanation.surface: A fear that was mistakenly called into question.
explanation.definitionFit: Defied someone to do something, as in a bold provocation.
